newsitem.title: USA: Apache sees February West Cameron output.
newsitem.headline: Apache sees February West Cameron output.

text.p: Apache Corp said Tuesday it ended 1996 with 19 indicated new-field or new-zone discoveries undergoing completion.

Included in this tally is the 50 percent-owned, Apache-operated platform on West Cameron 615 in the Gulf of Mexico where natural gas production is due to come on line in February at a rate of 40 to 50 million cubic feet per day.
It noted six other Gulf of Mexico 3-D prospects are drilling or undergoing completion operations.
"We boosted our drilling budget late last year and are beginning to feel the impact," Apache said.
"This year we're looking for an even higher level of exploration and development activity to push production toward our goal of 650 MMcf of gas and 75,000 barrels of oil per day."

"We're on track with our strategy of concentrating on the drillbit," said President and Chief Operating Officer G. Steven Farris. "We participated in 385 wells in 1996, making it the most active drilling year in the company's history."
In North America at year end Apache had 69 wells working, 38 of which were in the process of completion. Of the latter, 21 appear to be predominantly gas and 17 primarily oil wells.

Apache's international operations continued to expand during 1996. At year end the company had seven wells drilling and four awaiting completion in Egypt, where one 3-D seismic crew is conducting a 56-square-mile survey and two 2-D crews are shooting 3,700 miles of seismic on portions of the 19 million gross acres held by Apache and its partners.
In Bohai Bay, People's Republic of China, two wells were under way at the close of 1996. Results are expected to be released within the next several weeks.
Production began in November on the Apache-operated East Spar block in the Carnarvon Basin, offshore Western Australia.

Sales are currently averaging 30 million cubic feet (MMcf) of gas and 2,000 barrels of condensate per day from two subsea wells approximately 40 miles from the company's production and processing facilities on Varanus Island.

Volumes are being marketed under three separate contracts, with two additional contracts under negotiation. Production is expected to increase to 40 MMcf of gas and 3,000 barrels of condensate daily by mid-1997.
Apache owns a 20 percent interest in the block. East Spar is expected to produce more than 3.6 billion cubic feet of gas equivalent this year.
Apache has awarded contracts for the fabrication of all production facilities at the offshore Stag oil field, approximately 80 miles from East Spar.

The field, with reserves estimated at more than 40 million barrels, is expected to be on stream by the end of 1997, producing at a rate of approximately 25,000 barrels per day. The company is the operator, with a 33 percent working interest.
